summary: Ars Technica reports that Epic Games released a public "Preview" of a rewritten Epic Games Launcher that it says was "vibe coded" with AI and is faster than Steam. Epic's Martin Keely says AI helped a small team rebuild the code base from scratch on a new tech stack for Windows, Mac and soon Linux. Ars's own testing found a cold start to the store page a few seconds faster than Steam, while a claimed 0.06-second advantage in restoring from the system tray was unnoticeable.
speakers_or_authors: Ars Technica staff writer (unnamed in the excerpt); quotes Epic Games Store GM/VP Martin Keely (via PC Gamer and IGN) and Epic's official announcement.
relevance_reason: This is about AI-assisted software development (vibe coding) and launcher speed, not about how people interact with computers through AI. It has no connection to personal context devices, computer-use agents or voice/conversational interfaces. It is off-topic for the publication.

claims.claim: Epic says it used AI to rewrite the launcher from scratch, replicating the functionality of the old one but not its code, on a different tech stack.
claims.quote: started from scratch” and used AI as “a tool to write and review new features and new capabilities from the ground up in a different tech stack

claims.claim: Ars's testing found the new launcher reaches the store page from a cold start a few seconds faster than Steam, while the claimed 0.06-second tray-restore advantage was unnoticeable.
claims.quote: Ars’s own testing confirms that the new Launcher goes from a cold start to the store page a few seconds faster than Steam

commercial_interest: Epic Games is the vendor describing its own product and using the speed claim competitively against Valve's Steam. Ars's independent testing partly checks the claims.
older_event: No. The item covers a launch on 2026-10-14, within 30 days of publication.
